artifacts.title: DeJong v. Session of Village Seven Presbyterian Church
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained in part and denied in part RE DeJong's complaint against Session of Village Seven Presbyterian Church (Rocky Mountain Presbytery), upholding Session's creation of a Judicial Commission and its recommendation to remove term limit restrictions for ruling elders, but annulling Session's creation of a Governance Commission because two provisions of the governing document unconstitutionally allowed the commission to function like the Session itself, exceeding the limits placed on commissions by BCO 15-1.

artifacts.title: Speck v. Missouri Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained in part and denied in part TE Ryan Speck's complaint against Missouri Presbytery's December 2019 adoption of six theological judgments regarding the 2018 Revoice Conference hosted by Memorial Presbyterian Church, ruling that MOP applied an incorrect constitutional standard (BCO 34-5 'vitals of religion') rather than the proper BCO 11-3, 11-4, and 13-9(f) criteria, and failed to take adequate action with respect to erroneous teachings identified by its own committees regarding terminology (TJ 2), the 'gay beneath the gay' (TJ 3), and spiritual friendships (TJ 5); the matter was remanded to MOP with instructions for a new hearing. Dissenting opinions were filed by RE John D. Pickering and TE David F. Coffin, Jr., who argued that the SJC improperly raised an issue not presented by either party in violation of BCO 39-3.1.

artifacts.title: Bethel v. Southeast Alabama Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled Case 2012-06 administratively out of order on two grounds: the complaint was not filed within the required 30-day period under BCO 43-2, and the complainant (a deacon who was not a commissioner to presbytery on the date of the action complained against) lacked standing under BCO 43-1.

artifacts.synopsis: Susan Elizabeth Spann filed an appeal alleging Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church committed excommunication without process and spiritual abuse, but the SJC dismissed the appeal as premature because there was no record of a judicial decision by OMPC nor any prior appeal to Evangel Presbytery as required by BCO 42-2. The SJC requested that Evangel Presbytery direct OMPC to provide a written response to Ms. Spann's concerns.

artifacts.title: Snapp v. James River Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Byron Snapp complained that James River Presbytery erred in sustaining the ordination examination of a candidate who held an 'anthropomorphic' view of creation days rather than literal 24-hour days. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the Presbytery acted within its constitutional authority to sustain the examination and that the 26th GA had not yet resolved the constitutional status of such views.

artifacts.synopsis: Complainants challenged Mississippi Valley Presbytery's approval of James Blaha's theological examination for ordination regarding his views on charismatic gifts. The Special Judicial Commission upheld the challenge regarding prophecy (finding Blaha's views allow possibility of continuing revelation contrary to WCF 1.1 and 6), but rejected the challenge regarding tongues (finding private prayer language use within bounds of 1974 Pastoral Letter). Commission ordered presbytery to note prophecy exception in minutes and instruct Blaha not to teach or preach this view.

Carmel Session complained that New Jersey Presbytery erred by adopting a resolution of Affirmations and Denials Regarding the Interpretation of Genesis One that denied the 24-hour-day view as the only acceptable interpretation. artifacts.synopsis: Mrs. Sandra Lovelace complained against Northeast Presbytery's decision not to proceed to trial against teaching and ruling elders, and its ruling that her subsequent complaints were out of order due to non-membership. The SJC (reversing the Judicial Panel) denied the first item but sustained the second, holding that jurisdiction properly invoked is not forfeited by a subsequent change in the complainant's membership status.

artifacts.synopsis: Virgil B. Roberts complained that New River Presbytery delayed dissolving his pastoral relationship after he resigned and the congregation concurred. The SJC sustained the complaint, concluding that Presbytery should have acted on the agreed request rather than withholding dissolution; three commissioners dissented concerning Presbytery's constitutional authority and pastoral discretion.

artifacts.title: CCB authority to review SJC compliance and prior decisions
artifacts.disposition: CCB declined to accede to the reference; SJC decisions are final decisions of the GA (BCO 15-5); CCB does not render opinions on previous SJC decisions; Adopted 8-0-0

matches.evidence: The CCB declined a reference from Highlands Presbytery, ruling it lacks authority to render opinions on prior SJC decisions, which are final decisions of the General Assembly.

artifacts.title: General Assembly authority to amend or delete an SJC concurring opinion

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that the GA may not amend the SJC's report by deleting a concurring opinion, since under BCO 15-5 an SJC decision is the final decision of the Assembly.

artifacts.title: GA handling of an SJC minority decision under BCO 15-5

matches.evidence: Proposed amendment to BCO 15-5 clarifying how the General Assembly handles an SJC minority decision was found not in conflict with the BCO.

artifacts.title: Overture to abolish the Standing Judicial Commission

matches.evidence: The CCB found the overture to abolish the SJC in conflict with BCO 14-1 and 15, and also unconstitutionally vague about the basis for alternative decisions.

artifacts.title: Proposed Procedure for Resolving Alleged Conflicts Between Scripture and the Constitution

matches.evidence: The CCB found Eastern Canada Presbytery's overture in conflict with the Constitution because it would allow a General Assembly to bypass constitutional processes and permit modification of commission reports.
